boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along the Village and downtown corridors south and west of Hendrix College, each paired with one publicly documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Order a Pizza Beside Campus
cards.subtitle: Ellis Avenue — The Village at Hendrix
cards.notes: Follow Ellis Avenue into the Village and stop for house-made pizza or gelato; the restaurant’s site confirms the address and daily service.
cards.short_summary: An all-ages pizzeria anchors a close-to-campus Village block.
cards.evidence_claim: La Pista Pizzeria is located at 1050 Ellis Avenue and serves pizza and gelato daily from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m.
cards.access_notes: The business lists opening hours of 11 a.m.–9 p.m. Monday through Sunday.

cards.title: Pause for Coffee on Front Street
cards.subtitle: Front Street — Downtown Conway
cards.notes: Walk the Front Street corridor to this downtown café; use the documented address when distinguishing it from other Blue Sail listings.
cards.short_summary: A café provides a clear destination on downtown’s principal north–south street.
cards.evidence_claim: Blue Sail Coffee operates at 1028 Front Street in Conway and offers coffee, breakfast items, pastries, and lunch food.
cards.access_notes: The ordering page lists 7 a.m.–3 p.m. Monday–Friday and 8 a.m.–3 p.m. Saturday–Sunday.

cards.title: Take a Bandstand Break
cards.subtitle: Front Street — Downtown Conway
cards.notes: Continue along Front Street for the covered Kris Allen Stage, park benches, and a picnic table documented by Conway Parks and Recreation.
cards.short_summary: A compact civic park turns a downtown block into an outdoor pause point.
cards.evidence_claim: Simon Park at 805 Front Street has a covered bandstand, park benches, and a picnic table.
cards.source_title: Simon Park – City of Conway, Arkansas
cards.access_notes: The city identifies the park and its amenities; contact the mayor’s office to reserve the bandstand.

cards.title: Make Oak Street a Lunch Stop
cards.subtitle: Oak Street — Downtown Conway
cards.notes: Turn onto Oak Street for a daytime sandwich-shop stop; check the posted schedule because service ends at 2 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A locally operated lunch counter gives the Oak Street block a specific daytime purpose.
cards.evidence_claim: Cross Creek Sandwich Shop is located at 1003 Oak Street and serves breakfast on Saturday plus lunch Monday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Cross Creek Sandwich Shop | Contact | Conway, AR
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are 11 a.m.–2 p.m. Monday–Friday and 8–10:30 a.m. plus 11 a.m.–2 p.m. Saturday.

cards.title: Start the Tiny Toads Tour
cards.subtitle: Oak Street — Downtown Conway
cards.notes: Use Rogers Plaza as the Oak Street starting point for the city’s Tiny Toads public-art route, then follow the numbered downtown stops.
cards.short_summary: The gateway plaza supplies a documented starting point for a self-guided art walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Conway’s official Tiny Toads Tour identifies Rogers Plaza at 920 Oak Street as stop 1 and the gateway to Downtown Conway.
cards.access_notes: The city’s downloadable tour map presents Rogers Plaza as an outdoor route stop.

cards.title: Read the County Through Its Collections
cards.subtitle: Locust Avenue — Courthouse Square
cards.notes: Turn onto Locust Avenue to examine regional objects, photographs, art, and archival materials inside the historic 1896 county jail.
cards.short_summary: A former jail now holds the county’s material and documentary history.
cards.evidence_claim: The Faulkner County Museum at 801 Locust Avenue occupies the historic 1896 jail and maintains historical, archival, art, image, and object collections.
cards.access_notes: The museum lists public hours of 9 a.m.–4 p.m. Monday through Thursday and recommends calling for information.

cards.title: See Local Government in Session
cards.subtitle: Main Street — Downtown Conway
cards.notes: Use the Main Street block for an open City Council meeting; verify the current agenda before entering the second-floor chambers.
cards.short_summary: City Hall offers a concrete civic reason to visit Main Street on meeting nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Conway City Council meetings are open to the public and ordinarily occur at 6 p.m. on the second and fourth Tuesdays at 1111 Main Street.
cards.access_notes: Check the city meeting page for rescheduling or cancellation; regular meetings begin at 6 p.m.

cards.title: Follow Conway’s Black History Markers
cards.subtitle: Markham Street — East Side historic corridor
cards.notes: Walk the Markham Street park path and read the granite markers honoring people and families connected to Conway’s East Side history.
cards.short_summary: A civic square interprets the historic African-American community through its landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: Martin Luther King Jr. Square at 1101 Markham Street includes a playground, Unity Sculpture, and granite historical markers about influential community members.
cards.source_title: Martin Luther King Jr. Square – City of Conway, Arkansas
cards.access_notes: The city lists the square as a public park; contact the mayor’s office for reservations.

cards.title: Use the County Library’s Shared Spaces
cards.subtitle: Tyler Street — west of downtown
cards.notes: Follow Tyler Street to browse shared collections or use public spaces and activities; consult the library calendar for scheduled programs.
cards.short_summary: The county system’s headquarters expands an off-campus study route beyond downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Conway library at 1900 Tyler Street is the headquarters of the county system and provides shared collections, spaces, and activities.
cards.source_title: Conway Public Library | Hours, Location & Services
cards.access_notes: Current posted hours are 9 a.m.–7 p.m. Monday–Thursday and 9 a.m.–5 p.m. Friday–Saturday; closed Sunday.

cards.title: Loop the Park’s Jogging Track
cards.subtitle: Robinson Avenue — west Conway corridor
cards.notes: Take Robinson Avenue to the park’s seven-tenths-mile jogging track, or use its open lawn, playground, picnic tables, and seasonal splash pad.
cards.short_summary: A 26-acre park adds an outdoor exercise destination to the westward route.
cards.evidence_claim: Laurel Park at 2310 Robinson Avenue covers 26 acres and includes a 0.7-mile jogging track, open space, playground, picnic facilities, and a seasonal splash pad.
cards.source_title: Laurel Park – City of Conway, Arkansas
cards.access_notes: The park is public; the city currently marks the splash-pad opening date as to be determined.
